# Review handbook navigation

## Approach and why

Read the two Markdown files that make up this member directly:
`repos/docs/README.md` and `repos/docs/AGENTS.md`, at revision
`d4ef4e5c401ae71d98d48b8d1cbe6b5198a26f0d`. `repos/docs/AGENTS.md` states the
member is plain Markdown only, that named files are to be reviewed with
existing file tools, and that no build or installation is needed. Both files
were inspected during this planning run and are short, so ordinary reads reach
complete coverage; there is no search gap to solve.

`repos/docs/README.md` names its own navigation gaps (glossary and review
owner). A useful review therefore has to confirm those against the file rather
than repeat the file's self-description, and state plainly what the two files
cannot establish — for example whether a glossary exists anywhere outside this
member.

## Guidance and tools

Recommendations are deliberately empty: add nothing. No asset in
`.docflow_workspace/integrations/sources.yaml` covers documentation. The
catalogued `react-review` checklist is scoped to React function components and
`desktop-notes` to Svelte and Rust; neither applies here, and substituting one
would be unsound. The React review's declined retrieval choice is specific to
that review and is not extended to this member.

- **Availability:** ordinary file reads are available and were exercised in this
  planning run; no asset needs to be present, enabled or installed.
- **Constraints:** no edits to this member during workspace planning; no
  release or deployment; no new tooling, per the workspace data policy.
- **Dependencies:** none. This review does not depend on the React or
  Svelte/Tauri reviews and can proceed alone.
- **Fallback:** if a file search tool is unavailable, open the two named files
  explicitly — the same coverage.
- **Check:** re-read both files at the recorded revision and confirm every
  reported gap resolves to a cited line, and that each remaining question is
  recorded as unknown.

## Authority

None recorded. Planning only; the blocker above names who would grant the
review and what that grant would have to cover.

# Review search input accessibility

## Approach and why

Read the named React files directly at revision
`e3830821e87533c1effe82bc17fb4c349302c988`: `repos/react/src/Search.tsx`,
`repos/react/guidance/react-review.md`, `repos/react/package.json` and
`repos/react/AGENTS.md`. `repos/react/AGENTS.md` requires the review to run
against the pinned checklist, so the checklist drives the structure of the
findings: hook ordering, controlled-input updates, and labels.

The component under review is two lines and is a single controlled input. That
size is why direct inspection is sufficient and why the review's value lies in
precision — citing the exact line for each checklist item, and being explicit
that whether a label is supplied by a caller, or by rendered context outside
this file, cannot be determined from `Search.tsx` alone.

## Guidance and tools

- **`react-review` checklist — referenced, selected.** Required by the member's
  own rules. Available and verified: the on-disk file hashes to the catalogued
  revision. Read-only guidance; referencing it installs and configures nothing.
- **`retrieval` — declined, retained unchanged.** The user declined optional
  retrieval for this review because direct file inspection suffices. Host,
  actor stack, source revision, scope and data policy are unchanged since that
  choice, so it is retained verbatim rather than re-proposed. `DATA-POLICY.md`
  independently records that optional retrieval installation was declined as
  unnecessary, and the catalogue entry's declared effects include installing
  local dependencies — which is not authorised here.
- **Reviewer role.** `.docflow_workspace/agents/reviewer.md` pins this same
  checklist revision and maps to a `claude-code` alias in brief mode. It is a
  portable role definition, not a native host configuration, and selecting it
  would grant nothing; it is noted here as context only.

Availability, constraints, dependencies, fallback and check:

- **Availability:** checklist `present` (read, hash-verified); retrieval
  `not_present` and not authorised to install.
- **Constraints:** no dependency additions or package file changes; no
  automated accessibility tooling, since adding one would require an
  unauthorised installation; data stays on this workstation except the existing
  authorised Anthropic inference route.
- **Dependencies:** none on the other two reviews. The checklist is the only
  asset dependency and it is already present.
- **Fallback:** if the checklist is unreadable at the pinned revision, fall back
  to the member's `AGENTS.md` plus ordinary reads, and record the gap — do not
  substitute `desktop-notes`, which is scoped to Svelte and Rust.
- **Check:** each checklist item resolves to a cited line in `Search.tsx`, and
  the accessible-name question is answered or recorded as unknown with the
  reason.

## Approach and why

Read the member directly at revision
`8bbe8348cff207dfcbfe50865756d87229bddf16`: `repos/desktop/src/App.svelte`,
`repos/desktop/src-tauri/Cargo.toml`, `repos/desktop/package.json`,

`folder` string to a text input and calls nothing; `src-tauri/` holds only
`Cargo.toml`, declaring `tauri = "2"` with no Rust source and no command
handler. So the "folder bridge" has a Svelte half that is reviewable from
files and a Rust half that, at this revision, is not present to review. The
most useful thing this review can produce is a precise account of that — not a
narrative about a boundary the files do not contain. `guidance/desktop-review.md`
asks for exactly this: explain what cannot be verified, and note that native
runtime review needs a qualified domain procedure.

- **`tauri-specialist` — deferred, unavailable.** The declared location does

- **`react-review` — declined, incompatible.** React-only guidance against a
  Svelte and Rust member. Recorded explicitly so it is not substituted.

Availability, constraints, dependencies, fallback and check:

- **Availability:** `desktop-notes` present and verified; `tauri-specialist`
  unavailable at its declared path; `react-review` present but incompatible.
- **Constraints:** no package changes, no bridge execution, no application
  launch; no project data to a new external service. These exclude every
  runtime means of checking the native boundary.

- **Fallback:** a file-evidence-only review using `desktop-notes` and ordinary

- **Check:** the findings cite lines for the Svelte binding, state that
  `src-tauri` contains only `Cargo.toml` at the reviewed revision, list the
  boundary questions left unanswered, and cite neither the React checklist nor
  an unloaded specialist procedure.

## Authority

None recorded. Planning only; the blockers above name who would grant the
review, what must be resolved first, and what remains out of reach without
separately authorised domain coverage.
